messages:
elaine: Heads up — seeing a bunch of long-running inference pods in us-west2 stuck Pending with vGPU requests. Fractional reservations (0.25/0.5) seem to be leaving little unusable fragments on nodes.

matt: Which nodes/rows? any evictions or errors in scheduler logs?

elaine: quick dump:```
NAME                          READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE             REQUESTS
inference-trl-0               0/1     Pending   0          3h    <none>           requests.gpu: 0.25
inference-rl-1               0/1     Pending   0          2h    <none>           requests.gpu: 0.25
inference-large-3            0/1     Running   0          10h   node-uk0-3        requests.gpu: 1
```
Lots of Pending with tiny fractional requests. Node-level allocation shows leftover 0.25 on multiple racks.

neeraj: Sounds like the scheduler's fractional packing path is rounding down available vGPU capacity when multi-tenant reservations + node-level reserved taints are present. We hit this before when taint+reserve gating left "ghosted" allocations. Any recent config changes?

elaine: We flipped the vgpu-allocator to strict mode last week (bestEffort=false) to avoid noisy neighbors. Might be interacting with node taint vgpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule.

ops-bot: Alert: us-west2 vGPU fragmentation > 65% for 30m. Affected namespaces: ml-infra, research.

rami: If the scheduler marks small allocations as "reserved" but doesn't bind when multiple tiny requests race, those reserved slots don't get recycled until a node-level reconciliation. Could be leaking SSD-backed ephemeral affinity too.

matt: Can you paste a short kube-scheduler debug excerpt?

elaine: logs:```
I0321 13:12:01.123456  12345 scheduler.go:512] "Attempting allocate" pod=inference-trl-0 requests={vgpu:0.25}
I0321 13:12:01.123758  12345 predicate.go:87] "Predicate failed" node=node-uk0-3 reason=NotEnoughVGPU
I0321 13:12:01.124001  12345 allocator.go:210] "Reserved slot but not bound" pod=inference-trl-0 node=node-uk0-3 txn=tx-8723
I0321 13:12:01.124120  12345 allocator.go:420] "Reservation leak detected" node=node-uk0-3 reserved=0.25
```

neeraj: That "Reserved slot but not bound" line is the smoking gun. If txn aborted due to PreBind webhook timeouts, the slot stays flagged. We also saw the same pattern when the webhook times out ~200ms. Any webhook latency spikes?

elaine: YES — the auth webhook had a transient 300ms GC hiccup at 13:12.

rami: Short-term workaround: run a coordinated node reschedule for the most impacted nodes to force reconciliation. E.g. `kubectl drain node-uk0-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then uncordon after pods reschedule. Risk: eviction will disrupt running large jobs.

matt: Could we run a non-disruptive repair first — a controller that scans reservation table and reclaims orphaned fractions? Maybe a cron job to call the scheduler's internal reclaim API for nodes with small unusable tails.

elaine: Agreed. I'll spin up a canary reclaim job in us-west2a that calls scheduler debug/reclaim for nodes with <=0.5 free but no schedulable fit.

scheduler-bot: Proposed config patch (canary):```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  vgpuAllocator.mode: "strict" -> "strict-with-reclaim"
  vgpuAllocator.reclaimInterval: "1m"
  vgpuAllocator.prebindTimeoutMs: "500"
```

rami: Two action items: 1) elaine — deploy reclaim cron in us-west2a and monitor fragmentation metric for 1 hour (ETA 30m). 2) neeraj/matt — add a prebind webhook timeout guard so reserved slots are rolled back on timeout instead of left in reserved state.

matt: add me for postmortem. Also suggest nightly defrag job that attempts binpack compaction during low-traffic windows (02:00-04:00). That should reduce unit cost too.

elaine: rolling canary now. I'll post results in 15m. Thanks all :thumbsup:
